 사진 확대 Taekwondo demonstrations are being held at the 78th anniversary of the Armed Forces Day event held on the runway of Gyeryongdae in Gyeryong-si, Chungcheongnam-do. [Saekyung DB] On the 7th, the People's Power strongly criticized the situation in which North Korea's sole registration of 'Tangwon' as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, saying, "What did the government do?"
 Ham In-kyung, a spokesman for People's Power, said in a commentary that "Taekwon, the flag of the Republic of Korea, is on the verge of being listed on UNESCO as an intangible heritage of North Korea," adding, "What can the people trust and entrust if the government cannot even keep the flag properly?"
 "What did our government do while North Korea was pursuing the registration of Taekwondo alone?," he said. "Should we also be wary of North Korea in protecting South Korea's cultural heritage?"
 사진 확대 The appearance of the Kukkiwon in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, on the 5th, when concerns about the impact on Korea's status as a suzerain state are raised as 技 Taekwondo has been virtually confirmed to be registered as a "traditional martial art of North Korea" on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. [Yonhap News] The National Heritage Administration's response was also sharpened.
 "What is even more surprising is the attitude of the National Heritage Administration," Ham said. "A private organization asked UNESCO to deliver an official letter explaining the legitimacy of the joint registration of Taekwondo before the announcement of the review results, but the National Heritage Administration said it did, while claiming that the organization did not actually deliver it."
 If this is true, it is an act of deceiving the people beyond simple negligence of work, he said. "The National Heritage Administration should clarify whether or not to send an official letter."
 He also emphasized, "The UNESCO listing of Taekwondo is not simply a matter of which country is listed," adding, "It is a matter of the history, legitimacy, and pride of Taekwondo that Korea has informed the world."
 In this regard, the National Heritage Administration recently issued a position and said, "It is regrettable that North Korea submitted an application for Taekwondo's sole registration to UNESCO in March 2024, but the former government did not respond or take effective measures."
 "Since the launch of the Lee Jae Myung government, the National Heritage Administration has deeply recognized the urgency of the issue and has been active to secure the status of our Taekwondo," he said. "In particular, after the leading coordination of the National Heritage Administration, a dramatic agreement was reached, and based on this, we were able to finally submit an application for Korean Taekwondo to UNESCO in March this year."
